title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion
summary: MILD-MT randomized 304 patients in China with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion, NIHSS less than 6, a small infarct core, and substantial perfusion mismatch within 24 hours to thrombectomy plus medical management or medical management alone; 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. Excellent 90-day outcome (mRS 0-1) occurred in 69.4% versus 50.0% (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.41-3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 3 patients in each group, while serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 of 144 thrombectomy patients (13.2%).
findings: mRS 0-1 at 90 days occurred in 69.4% with thrombectomy versus 50.0% with medical management alone (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.41-3.81; P<0.001).
Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group.
Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 of 144 thrombectomy patients (13.2%).
One death occurred among all participants, in the thrombectomy group.
population: Patients with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion ischemic stroke, NIHSS less than 6, small infarct core, and substantial perfusion mismatch within 24 hours.
shortTitle: MILD-MT: thrombectomy for mild-deficit LVO stroke
limitations: The study was open-label, conducted in China, and selected patients using small-core and large-perfusion-mismatch imaging criteria. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 13.2%, and applicability outside the studied population remains uncertain.
whyItMatters: The trial challenges a default medical-management approach for mild-deficit LVO when perfusion imaging shows substantial tissue at risk. For a highly selected patient with mild symptoms and LVO, early thrombectomy-center consultation is more defensible, but these data do not support indiscriminate EVT for every low-NIHSS LVO.
evidenceNotes: Abstract reviewed; full text unavailable. Primary PubMed record and DOI metadata were verified.
primaryEndpoint: Excellent functional outcome, defined as modified Rankin scale 0 or 1, at 90 days.
